title: scottish power make 15 billion upgrade britains largest onshore wind farm 2026 07 22
text:
LONDON, July 22 (Reuters) - Iberdrola-owned (IBE.MC)
, opens new tab
 Scottish Power is investing £1.5 billion ($2.01 billion) ‌to upgrade old turbines at the Whitelee Windfarm in Scotland, a move that will almost double capacity at Britain's largest onshore windfarm, it said on Wednesday.
Britain plans to rapidly increase its renewable ​power capacity to help meet climate targets, boost energy security and reduce the ​country’s reliance on imported fossil fuels.
Under the repowering plan, the 215 ⁠existing turbines at Whitelee will be replaced with 124 larger turbines that will ​almost double the project's capacity to around 1 gigawatt, enough electricity to power around ​650,000 homes.
"We will repower it in sections over that period of time, and that means we still get the best out of the existing site as we start building the new site," Scottish ​Power CEO Keith Anderson said in an interview.
Anderson said the project would start ​around 2030 and be complete by around 2035.
Wind turbines are typically designed to operate for around ‌20 to ⁠25 years, and many older projects are coming to the end of their lifespan.
As well as owning generation and network assets, Scottish Power is one of Britain’s largest energy suppliers.
Anderson welcomed the move by Britain’s new Prime ​Minister Andy Burnham ​on Monday to remove VAT ⁠from domestic electricity bills to help consumers with a cost of living squeeze, but said more will need to be done ​to help reduce soaring energy debts.
"We need to take away ​some of ⁠that old debt burden because people clearly just can't afford to pay it," Anderson said. "Put it into a fund, securitise the fund, and have that fund repaid over 10-15 ⁠years."
Industry group ​Energy UK predicts household energy debt could hit £7 ​billion by the end of the year.
Anderson was speaking after parent company Iberdrola announced a 22% rise in first-half ​net profits to €4.34 billion ($4.95 billion).
